state: offline preregistered measurement plan; no performance acceptance
question: Does removing scheduler-selection replay improve complete execution across private post-resume demands at unchanged retained capacity?
hypothesis: Removing duplicate/unscheduled selection sweeps can reduce trigger work and interference; losing useful late replay may instead hurt. No gain is assumed.

boot_plan.each_cell: fresh power-recovered boot, global flock retained through recovery; release between sessions for other owners

primary_endpoint: control-minus-old change in paired off-on whole-cell benefit; allocation/fork/warmup/checks/reaping/frees/resource observation included
secondary_endpoint: paired complete two-switch steady transaction, including kernel trigger work/interference
resources: actual whole-cell OS faults/switches/user/system counters; not cache-miss proxies
analysis: dedicated fixed-image comparator; >=2 independent complete boots per image; same config/ELF/transfer/bitstream, hierarchical resampling boots then paired blocks
failure_policy: Preserve native timeout, transfer/kernel/terminal failures and recover before lock release; never accept partial rows. No count-based or performance-based stopping/cherry-picking inside an accepted boot.
interpretation_limits: Counter pilots10/11 have different ELF and loop counts and are not pooled with performance runs.
No new retained capacity, address table, rootfs or hardware is introduced by this pair.
A single workload or unreplicated boot cannot establish general application benefit.
If whole-cell cost regresses despite a local/steady gain, reject the optimization claim.
